- **self**: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts (7/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Treat routing readiness as a separate condition from Case lifecycle alert eligibility. This is an architectural inference: Omni-Channel applies routing logic when work is assigned to an owner and does not reapply it after later field edits; PendingServiceRouting describes work waiting for routing or assignment. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/service/service-presence-developer-guide/guide/omnichannel-developer-guide-intro.html · keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/object-reference/references/standard-objects/object-pendingservicerouting.html
- [statement] For queue-based routing, PendingServiceRouting creation does not invoke before-insert or after-insert triggers, or actions such as triggers, workflow rules, or validation that could interfere with record creation. A design that expects an insert trigger on this routing record to deliver every alert conflicts with this documented behavior. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/object-reference/references/standard-objects/object-pendingservicerouting.html · keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The routing object's readiness flag describes readiness to route work to an agent; when true, the PendingServiceRouting record cannot be edited. This is routing readiness, not evidence that a Case lifecycle alert has been delivered. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/object-reference/references/standard-objects/object-pendingservicerouting.html · keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts
- [statement] In a historical Stack Exchange report, a Case user said changing Status to Open or New did not resolve the reported routing-record creation failure. This is an attributed observation, not a verified current Salesforce defect. (low confidence) — https://salesforce.stackexchange.com/questions/377548/field-integrity-exception-cant-create-pendingservicerouting-object-because-the/382112 · keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts
- [statement] PendingServiceRouting readiness indicates whether a work item is ready to be routed to an agent; once true, the PendingServiceRouting record cannot be edited. It does not by itself attest that an agent has accepted the work. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/object-reference/references/standard-objects/object-pendingservicerouting.html · keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Do not interpret the routing-versus-lifecycle distinction as saying that work status never affects Omni-Channel. Status-based capacity measures accepted-work status, and optional capacity checks before reopening or reassigning work can reroute work when the rep lacks capacity. (low confidence) — https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.omnichannel_status_based_capacity.htm&language=en_US&type=5 · keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

## Facts and statements

- [statement] External-routing notifications have a routing-specific lifecycle: new work is sent to the partner application, which matches it to logged-in reps; Salesforce also notifies the partner after acceptance, decline, completion, and rep logout. These documented milestones should not be assumed to enumerate every later Case field change. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/service/service-presence-developer-guide/guide/omnichannel-external-routing-flow.html · keywords: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

## Research summary — Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts

Omni-Channel readiness concerns routing work to an agent. Salesforce states that later field changes do not reapply routing logic. External routing exposes work-acceptance, decline and completion notifications, but those milestones do not establish coverage of every Case lifecycle change. Treat routing readiness and alert delivery as separate checks. A historical Case routing-error report illustrates why a visible Case status alone does not prove routing succeeded. The forum observation remains attributed and does not establish a current defect.
